description: deixis mandatory Node[T] identity vectors — structural equality of ADR 0010 §3 (n ≡ m iff D_n = D_m and v_n(p) ≈ v_m(p) at every p ∈ D_n, with v TOTAL on D). Every case declares its slot: the carrier and its ≈, as defined in vectors/MNODE-PLAN.md. Hand-authored from docs/design/0010-mandatory-node-values.md, docs/TREE.md and docs/PATH.md as merged in 1a9bb6d, and from nothing else. No implementation of the mandatory API existed when these were written, so none can have been copied. Items X7–X10 and X19; each note names the defect (W) it catches. 24 cases.

cases.name: m-fixture-same-class-different-representation
cases.note: X7. The fixture ≈ compares class only, so two childless nodes with ≈ values are equal.

cases.name: m-fixture-different-class
cases.note: X7. v(ε) differ under ≈.

cases.name: m-fixture-root-value-differs-over-identical-children
cases.note: X7, X11. Identical children, different root values: TREE says a parent's own value is never inferred from its children. Catches W5 (terminal-only comparison) and W9.

cases.name: m-fixture-interior-value-differs-only
cases.note: X7. Same paths; the only difference is v([6b]), the value of an interior node, which has a child of its own. ≈ applies at every node, not only terminal ones. Catches W5.

cases.name: m-fixture-interior-differs-only-in-representation
cases.note: X7. The coarse ≈ holds at the interior node as well: the relation is used at every node, and it ignores representation there too.

cases.name: m-fixture-sibling-order-irrelevant
cases.note: X7. The children are a finite map; TREE says sibling order is not part of a node.

cases.name: m-fixture-extra-child
cases.note: X7. D_left = {ε,[61]} and D_right = {ε,[61],[62]}: key domains must be equal.

cases.name: m-fixture-childless-vs-one-child-same-value
cases.note: X7. TREE, 'What identity is not': deixis does not decide that a node with descendants equals a childless node, even when every value present is ≈.

cases.name: m-fixture-empty-key-is-a-key
cases.note: X19. D_left = {ε, [""]}: the empty key is a key, and the path [""] is not ε (ADR 0010 §3: empty key and empty path differ).

cases.name: m-fixture-keys-are-exact-bytes
cases.note: X19. Keys are exact byte strings: ff and ff00 differ by a trailing zero byte. Neither is valid UTF-8, which does not matter.

cases.name: m-option-none-vs-some-empty
cases.note: X8. With tag-respecting option equality, none differs from some(e), even when e is the fixture's own empty value (TREE, 'Optionality is a slot choice'). Catches W6.

cases.name: m-option-none-vs-none
cases.note: X8. none ≈ none. Both are existing childless nodes carrying the payload none.

cases.name: m-option-some-coarse-inside
cases.note: X8. some(x) ≈ some(y) iff x ≈ y, and the fixture ≈ ignores representation.

cases.name: m-option-paths-retained-under-none
cases.note: X10. PATH, 'Identity, extensionally', gives exactly this pair: the path [61] exists on the left although its payload is none. A none payload is not a missing node. Catches W3.

cases.name: m-option-interior-none-vs-some
cases.note: X8, X7. The only difference is the interior node's payload, none against some(i). Catches W5 and W6 together.

cases.name: m-unit-same-paths-any-order
cases.note: X9. Node[Unit] is pure keyed shape (ADR 0010 §1): every value is the unit, so identity is equality of path domains.

cases.name: m-unit-different-paths
cases.note: X9. Different path domains.

cases.name: m-unit-childless-vs-one-child
cases.note: X9. D_left = {ε} and D_right = {ε,[61]}. Every value is ≈, so the domains alone decide.

cases.name: m-json-null-vs-null
cases.note: X4. null is a legal payload of the json slot, and an existing childless node carries it.

cases.name: m-json-null-vs-false
cases.note: X4. Structural JSON equality separates null from false; no payload is special to the core.

cases.name: m-json-null-vs-empty-object
cases.note: X4. Under the json slot, {} is an ordinary JSON object and differs from null. Under the unit slot the same spelling is the unit. The declared slot decides, never the spelling alone.

cases.name: m-json-object-member-order-ignored
cases.note: X7. The json slot's ≈ ignores object member order (MNODE-PLAN, slots).

cases.name: m-json-null-child-is-an-existing-node
cases.note: X4, X10. The child at [61] holds a null payload and still exists: D_left = {ε,[61]}. TREE, 'Existing versus missing': no payload denotes a missing path. Catches W3.

cases.name: m-json-null-interior-vs-string
cases.note: X4, X7. The interior values are the JSON null and the string "null", which differ. The comparison happens at an interior node.
